---
title: '<span style = "font-size: 18pt!important;">The screening effects of naturalization costs</span>'
subtitle: '<a href = "https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/1ab4ya0yajco3ssh9aq96/Govind_Sirugue_2026_Screening_effect_naturalization.pdf?rlkey=fol3cha7fagit87l49vzxo0og&st=7kwcewbw&e=2&dl=0" target="_blank"><span style = "color:#18BC9C!important;">Latest version</span></a>, <i>with <a href = "https://sites.google.com/view/yajnagovind/home" target="_blank"><span style = "color:#18BC9C!important;">Yajna Govind</span></a>, <b>R&R at Journal of Public Economics</b></i>'
abstract: '<span style = "color:#6C757D;">We study how changing citizenship costs affect naturalization decisions and the skill composition of naturalized immigrants. We develop a theoretical framework in which benefits from citizenship are heterogeneous and costs vary with skills. We test its predictions in a quasi-experimental setting, exploiting the abolition of compulsory conscription in France as a reduction in the citizenship costs for sons of immigrants. We find that naturalization costs are higher for the low-educated, such that compulsory conscription induced positive selection on education within benefit groups. It also led to positive selection across benefit groups, which, as shown theoretically, is not guaranteed.</span>'
